source_checks.note: Read the complete USDA/FSA 2024 report and manually inspected the relevant tables. It supports approximately 46 million foreign-held acres, 3.6% of privately held agricultural land and roughly 2% of all US land; China 247,659 acres, Iran 547, Russia 11, North Korea 0; the five-company 92% decomposition; no filings directly by China's government; lease/wind predominance; the minimum-count caveat; and the 2025 penalty figures. The Report 12 table visually aligns $120,216.38 with Brazos Highland, discharging the requested human glance.

GAO-24-106337 supports the article's AFIDA data-quality findings: manual and incomplete processes, inadequate verification and quality review, double-counting, and DOD/CFIUS access and timeliness gaps.

The June 25, 2026 Federal Register document is a proposed, not final, AFIDA modernization rule and supports the quoted description of USDA's transaction-specific CFIUS participation. The essay preserves the proposal status.
The 2023 AFIDA report supports the article's vintage comparison: 277,336 China-associated acres, Texas 123,708, Utah 33,035, and no filings directly by China's government.
Florida's official statute supports the covered-person definition and the one-residence, two-acre, five-mile, valid-visa exception, together with grandfathering and registration provisions.
The enrolled Texas SB 17 text supports the article's description of the enacted Texas restriction and its September 1, 2025 effective date.
Treasury's final CFIUS rule supports the Grand Forks Air Force Base 100-mile-radius jurisdictional expansion and its December 9, 2024 effective date.
The Mayer Brown client alert supports the narrow point that CFIUS determined it lacked jurisdiction over the Fufeng transaction under the rules then in force.

Foreign Policy contains the article's exact quoted explanation that CFIUS review was limited because the Blue Hills project was a greenfield investment. The body attributes that exact quotation to Texas Public Radio instead; this source mismatch is publication-blocking even though the substantive explanation is supported.

This syndication preserves the same Foreign Policy story and exact CFIUS quotation, further identifying the quotation's provenance. No corresponding full Texas Public Radio article was found from the ledger's title/date description.
Forbes supports the attributed account of Sun Guangxin's Val Verde County holdings and business background. The essay treats the security assessment as attributed rather than independently proven.
CBS supports the Fondomonte/Arizona groundwater and lease-termination example. It is used as a conduct-based regulatory comparison, not as evidence about Chinese ownership.

OPB supports the attributed Tianqiao Chen Oregon acquisition and the discrepancy between land-ranking coverage and AFIDA classification. The essay correctly labels its proposed reclassification explanation as hypothesis.
The Land Report profile supports the attributed acreage/ranking used in the Chen comparison; it does not establish AFIDA classification.
Al Jazeera supports the reported annual agricultural-purchase commitment. The article carries it as a reported agreement claim, not a completed-purchases fact.

hold_reasons: A load-bearing quotation about CFIUS's Blue Hills jurisdiction is attributed in the body to Texas Public Radio, but the exact language is traceable to Foreign Policy and its syndication; the named Texas Public Radio source could not be located.
The source ledger itself requires full fetch before external publication, so an unresolved outlet/quotation mismatch cannot be promoted by merely preserving the underlying substantive point.
unresolved_obligations: Correct the body and source ledger to the actual source of the CFIUS quotation, or supply and digest-bind the missing Texas Public Radio full text showing the exact language.
